# Part 1: Legacy of redlining in current environmental (in)justice

## Load Packages and Source Functions

```{r}
library(sf)
library(tmap)
library(tidyverse)
library(spData)
library(stars)
library(here)
library(bit64)

install.packages("sf")
install.packages("stars")
install.packages("tmap")
```

## Import Data

```{r}
#Import HOLC data as LA_Inequality
LA_Inequality <- sf::st_read(here::here("data", "mapping-inequality","mapping-inequality-los-angeles.json"))

#Import ej screen for LA inequalities
ejscreen <- sf::st_read(here::here("data", "ejscreen","EJSCREEN_2023_BG_StatePct_with_AS_CNMI_GU_VI.gdb"))

california <- ejscreen |>
  dplyr::filter(ST_ABBREV == "CA")

los_angeles <- ejscreen |>
  dplyr::filter(CNTY_NAME %in% c("Los Angeles County"))
```

Data wrangle LA inequalities and HOLC grade map
```{r}
#Transform LA_Inequality to same crs as los_angeles
Inequality_transform <- st_transform(LA_Inequality, crs = st_crs(los_angeles))

#Combine LA_Inequality with los_angeles
Combined_LA <- st_join(los_angeles, Inequality_transform, left = TRUE)
```

Map of historical redlining neighborhoods
```{r}
tm_shape(Combined_LA,bbox = LA_Inequality) +
    tm_polygons(fill="grade",
    fill.scale = tm_scale(values = c("burlywood4", "lightsalmon2", "brown3","brown4","honeydew3")),
    fill.legend = tm_legend(title = "Redlining Grade")
    )
```

Create percentage summary table of each HOLC block
```{r}
#Replace na values with NoGrade
Combined_LA <- Combined_LA |> replace_na(list(grade = "NoGrade"))

#Create table
PercentTable <- Combined_LA |>
  count(grade) |> 
  st_drop_geometry()

PercentTable <- PercentTable |> 
  mutate(n = (100*(n/sum(PercentTable$n)))) |> 
  rename(Percent = n)

PercentTable
```

Low percent income and Percentile Particulate Matter 2.5 within HOLC grades
```{r}
OnlyHOLC <- st_join(Inequality_transform, los_angeles, left = TRUE)

LI_and_PM_table <- OnlyHOLC |>
  group_by(grade) |>
  summarize(LowIncomePercent = mean(LOWINCPCT),
            PercentilePM2.5 = mean(P_PM25)) |>
  st_drop_geometry()

LI_and_PM_table <- LI_and_PM_table |> 
  mutate(LowIncomePercent = LowIncomePercent*100)

LI_and_PM_table <- LI_and_PM_table |>
  pivot_longer(!grade, names_to = "Measure", values_to = "Percentile")

ggplot(LI_and_PM_table, aes(fill=Measure, y=Percentile, x=grade)) + 
    geom_bar(position="dodge", stat="identity")
```

- Result reflection -

Towards the southeast, there seems to higher percentile of particulate matter 2.5, which seems to be generally correlated with a higher redlining grade. Similarly, percent low income also seems to increase as redlining grade goes up. The redlining of these areas may be causational of their low income and particulate matter pollution status.

# Part 2: Legacy of redlining in pedstrian and bike accidents

## Load data

```{r}
Crashes_raw <- st_read(here::here("data", "SWITRS_LA","Crashes.csv"))
```

## Data wrangle of percent bike or pedestrian crashes in each HOLC region
```{r}
#Filter pedestrian or bicycle accidents
Crashes_peds_bikes <- Crashes_raw |>
  filter(PEDESTRIAN_ACCIDENT == "Y" | BICYCLE_ACCIDENT == "Y") |> 
  filter(POINT_X != 'NA')

# Which columsn have more NA's
sum((Crashes_raw$POINT_X == 'NA'))
sum((Crashes_raw$LATITUDE == 'NA'))

# We'll use xy

#Convert X and Y columns to points, using WGS 84, or code 4326
Crash_pb_trans <- st_as_sf(Crashes_peds_bikes, coords = c("POINT_X", "POINT_Y"), crs = 4326)

#Check CRS is correct
st_crs(Crash_pb_trans)

#Transform crash dots to HOLC map CRS
st_crs(Crash_pb_trans) == st_crs(OnlyHOLC)
Crash_trans_correct <- st_transform(Crash_pb_trans, crs = st_crs(OnlyHOLC))

# Subset points only within HOLC regions
HOLC_Crashes <- Crash_trans_correct[OnlyHOLC, ]

#Left join 
Crashes_left_join <- st_join(HOLC_Crashes, OnlyHOLC) |>
  select(id = ID, region = grade)

# Summarise HOLC grades with most crashes
Crashes_Table <- Crashes_left_join |>
  filter(!is.na(region)) |> 
  group_by(region) %>%
  summarise(n_points = n()) |>
  st_drop_geometry()

Crashes_percent <- Crashes_Table |> 
  mutate(Percentage = 100*(n_points/sum(Crashes_Table$n_points)))
Crashes_percent$region <- as.factor(Crashes_percent$region)
Crashes_percent$Percentage <- as.double(Crashes_percent$Percentage)

Crashes_percent
```

## Visualize data
```{r}
ggplot(Crashes_percent, aes(x = region, y = Percentage, fill = region)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
  labs(x = "HOLC region", y = "% of bike and pedestrian crashes") +
  theme_minimal()
```
